mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the observed mean return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically distinguishable from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by >1.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average by more than 5% indicates a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market gains over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-month MA by >5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month—indicating population reclassification effects rather than true labor market tightening—predicts muted equity market reaction over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is statistically below zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals a prolonged low-growth environment, which erodes earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.
